topic: How does the hierarchical classification framework impact satellite link budget margins when prioritizing QoS-sensitive traffic?
consensus_response: Hierarchical classification simplifies management but sacrifices QoS accuracy due to traffic aggregation. This leads to underestimation of latency and jitter's impact on real-time QoS on satellite links, causing budget overruns and degraded user experience.  Satellite links inherently suffer from high latency and variable bandwidth, which are not adequately captured by aggregate-based prioritization. This mismatch between QoS promises and actual link performance directly impacts budget and service quality.
reference_context: Satellite links experience high latency and variable bandwidth, hindering the accuracy of QoS provisioning.  Hierarchical classification, while simplifying management, sacrifices QoS accuracy by neglecting link-specific characteristics like latency and jitter. This leads to budget overruns and degraded user experience due to the inherent challenges of satellite communication.
